title: HFPO-DA exacerbates acute ischemic stroke outcomes in rats via the CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
authors: Jia, Fang; Chen, Di; Huang, Ziyuan; Wan, Chengjie; Li, Ziyan; Huang, Tengchao; Gao, Shuangqi; Guo, Ying
one_liner_zh: 该文研究塑料添加剂HFPO-DA通过CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB信号通路加重大鼠缺血性脑卒中，分子对接仅用于预测小分子-蛋白结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: The incidence of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) has shown a persistent upward trend in recent years. External factors, including chemical and plastic exposures, have been shown to worsen the prognosis of cerebrovascular diseases, especially AIS. Hexafluoropropylene oxide dimer acid (HFPO-DA), a prevalent plastic additive, is globally distributed. However, its bioaccumulation potential and neurovascular toxicity remain poorly understood. Using a mixed subchronic-acute aggravation model in middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) rats, we found that HFPO-DA exposure dose-dependently exacerbated neurological deficits, enlarged infarct volumes, and intensified reactive microgliosis. Computationally, we prioritized the CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB signaling axis as a key mechanistic candidate, with bindings predicted by molecular docking. In vitro cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) coupled with targeted siRNA knockdown in BV2 cells supported a direct physical interaction between HFPO-DA and CSNK2A1. Moreover, in vivo CSNK2A1 inhibition with CX-4945 partially reversed the HFPO-DA-induced aggravation of ischemic injury. Collectively, our results suggest that HFPO-DA might be a potent environmental driver of post-ischemic neuroinflammation, likely acting in part via the CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB signaling pathway. These results provide novel insights into the specific neurotoxic mechanisms of HFPO-DA, highlighting its potential health risks in susceptible populations.
abstract_zh: 近年来，急性缺血性卒中（acute ischemic stroke, AIS）的发病率呈持续上升趋势。外部因素，包括化学物质和塑料暴露，已被证明会恶化脑血管疾病，尤其是AIS的预后。六氟环氧丙烷二聚酸（HFPO-DA）作为一种普遍存在的塑料添加剂，在全球范围内分布广泛。然而，其生物累积潜力及神经血管毒性仍知之甚少。利用大脑中动脉闭塞/再灌注（MCAO/R）大鼠的混合亚慢性-急性加重模型，我们发现HFPO-DA暴露剂量依赖性地加重了神经功能缺损、扩大了梗死体积，并加剧了反应性小胶质细胞增生。在计算层面，我们优先将CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB信号轴确定为关键机制候选，并通过分子对接预测了其结合。体外细胞热稳定性测定（CETSA）结合BV2细胞中的靶向siRNA敲低实验，支持HFPO-DA与CSNK2A1之间存在直接物理相互作用。此外，体内使用CX-4945抑制CSNK2A1可部分逆转HFPO-DA诱导的缺血性损伤加重。总体而言，我们的结果表明，HFPO-DA可能是缺血后神经炎症的一种强效环境驱动因素，其作用部分可能通过CSNK2A1/GSK3B/NF-kappaB信号通路介导。这些结果为HFPO-DA的特定神经毒性机制提供了新见解，并强调了其在易感人群中的潜在健康风险。
